conventions.convention: The local algorithms use zero-based knots t_i = ξ_{i+1} and coefficients indexed from zero. Nonempty evaluation spans satisfy p ≤ k ≤ n−1.
Knot cells are left-closed and right-open; interior-knot values come from the right cell, and the right endpoint b uses the left limit. Zero-denominator Cox–de Boor terms are zero.
Single-knot insertion accepts only a new knot strictly inside a nonempty span; insertion at an existing knot is outside its contract. Degree zero is allowed and has an empty blend range.
Clamped interpolation means C² piecewise cubics with prescribed endpoint slopes, using one-sided endpoint derivatives.
Floating-point success requires every exact intermediate to be zero or normal; nonzero subnormal results and overflow cause failure. Exact zeros are preserved.

Stored knots and values are the exact interpolation data. Certificate calculations use exact rational arithmetic; assembly discrepancies are included, while input conversion and rounded evaluation of the cubic pieces are excluded.
Arbitrary replacement nodal second derivatives define a piecewise-cubic reconstruction that need not be C¹. Its comparison with the exact natural interpolant is restricted to the knot hull.

The fourth-order clamped estimate assumes continuous derivatives through order four near the interval and endpoint slopes equal to the exact derivatives of the target function; arbitrary partitions are allowed.

load_bearing.statement: For stored data, assemble the rounded tridiagonal system, perform failure-aware bidiagonal Cholesky and substitutions, evaluate a rounded residual, and compute exact rational certificates C, α, β and B = H²(C + αQ + β)/(8δ). The r = 2 branch returns the straight-line reconstruction with B = 0.

On a supplied admissible knot span, initialize the p+1 active coefficients and perform the specified descending-index de Boor blends, using exact arithmetic or the stated failure-aware rounded operation order.

Insert a new knot u strictly inside a nonempty span, copying controls through k−p, blending Q_i = α_iP_i + (1−α_i)P_{i−1} for k−p+1 ≤ i ≤ k with α_i = (u−t_i)/(t_{i+p}−t_i), and shifting the remaining controls.
For the same nodal values and zero endpoint second derivatives, if E is the maximum nodal second-derivative discrepancy, then the reconstructed pieces satisfy ‖ŝ−s‖∞ ≤ H²E/8 on [x₁,x_r].
For r ≥ 3, δ = min(h_{i−1}+h_i) and exact residual ρ = A m̂−b, the reconstruction with zero endpoint second derivatives satisfies ‖ŝ−s‖∞ ≤ H²‖ρ‖∞/(8δ) on the knot hull.

Successful assembly produces an SPD matrix T. Every full successful call certifies ‖T m̂−f‖∞ ≤ C. Stronger, separately stated roundoff conditions give factor and triangular-solve backward bounds. The procedure terminates with O(r) floating-point and exact rational operations and storage, without a rational bit-complexity claim.
The exact-arithmetic de Boor procedure returns the degree-p B-spline coefficient expansion on the supplied half-open span, and its left limit at b when the last nonempty span is supplied.
For every 0 ≤ q ≤ p, every old basis index and every x ∈ [a,b], B_{i,q,t}(x) = λ_i^(q) B_{i,q,t′}(x) + (1−λ_{i+1}^(q)) B_{i+1,q,t′}(x), with the stated piecewise insertion weights.
For vector controls and one new knot strictly inside a nonempty span, the old and refined B-spline expansions agree at every x ∈ [a,b].

For any strictly increasing partition with m ≥ 1, arbitrary nodal values and prescribed endpoint slopes, there is exactly one clamped cubic interpolant; its nodal second derivatives solve the displayed endpoint-augmented tridiagonal system.

concerns.concern: F1 describes the natural cubic piece formula as “given by the displayed formula in its Statement.” In the cited thm-natural-cubic-interpolant-exists-uniquely-at-distinct-knots, the explicit cubic formula is in Proof step 2.1; the Statement displays the tridiagonal system. The argument uses the correct formula, but the locator is inaccurate.
